Its structure contains an ionizable piperidine and several polar functionalities but is not an obvious extreme BBB non-penetrant. The experimental result therefore outweighs any more favorable physicochemical intuition: whatever mechanism limits its CNS exposure is real. Because the transfer score is high and the query shares relevant ionization and heteroatom features, that measured phenotype has strong implications for the query.

The pattern continues at 0.7708 and 0.7603, where biodistribution and brain-to-blood measurements again show poor CNS exposure. Both molecules retain substantial hydrophobic/aromatic character, demonstrating experimentally that lipophilicity alone does not ensure brain penetration when other liabilities such as ionization, polarity, size, or transporter recognition intervene.
